headline: World Cup's 1,000th match: Japan rout Tunisia 4-0
summary: Japan becomes the first Asian side to score four goals in a single World Cup match, pushing Tunisia out of the tournament.
details: Japan secured a commanding 4-0 victory over Tunisia in the World Cup's 1,000th match on Saturday, moving closer to the knockout stages.
Daichi Kamada opened the scoring early in the fourth minute, followed by Ayase Ueda, who scored twice, including a fierce low drive in the 30th minute.
Junya Ito added a third goal after being set up by Ueda, before Ueda completed his own brace with a header from a deep cross.
With this win, Japan becomes the first Asian team to ever score four goals in a single World Cup match.
Tunisia, playing their first game under new coach Herve Renard, were eliminated from the tournament after a second successive defeat in Group F.
Japan now joins the Netherlands on four points in the group, while Tunisia joins Haiti and Turkey as the tournament's third eliminated side.
caption:
A historic milestone! Japan becomes the first Asian side to score 4 goals in a single World Cup match.

Japan secured a commanding 4-0 victory over Tunisia in the World Cup's 1,000th match on Saturday, moving closer to the knockout stages.

Daichi Kamada opened the scoring early in the fourth minute, followed by Ayase Ueda, who scored twice, including a fierce low drive in the 30th minute.

Junya Ito added a third goal after being set up by Ueda, before Ueda completed his own brace with a header from a deep cross.

With this win, Japan becomes the first Asian team to ever score four goals in a single World Cup match.

Tunisia, playing their first game under new coach Herve Renard, were eliminated from the tournament after a second successive defeat in Group F.

Japan now joins the Netherlands on four points in the group, while Tunisia joins Haiti and Turkey as the tournament's third eliminated side.

headline: BDT 119cr scam: Ex-MP Masud Uddin remanded for 4 days
summary: The former lawmaker and retired Lieutenant General is accused of embezzling over BDT 119 crore by illegally charging workers for deployment to Malaysia.
details: A Dhaka court has placed former MP Lieutenant General (Retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury on a four-day remand in connection with an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) case involving the embezzlement of over BDT 119 crore.
caption:
BDT 119 crore embezzled! Ex-MP Masud Uddin is now on a 4-day remand.

A Dhaka court has placed former MP Lieutenant General (Retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury on a four-day remand in connection with an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) case involving the embezzlement of over BDT 119 crore.
